Let \(p=4t+3\) and set \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Since \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\) and \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\), while \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\), we have \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Hence
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)\mid m\). Conversely, if \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m\), this implies \(2m\mid2n\), hence \(m\mid n\). Therefore \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\). Then
\[
a^m=(-1)^m(-a)^m\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
because \(m\) is odd. Also \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \((-a)^{2n}=a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\); write \(n=mq\). Now
\[
1\equiv a^n=(a^m)^q\equiv(-1)^q\pmod p.
\]
As \(p\) is odd, this forces \(q\) to be even. Hence \(2m\mid n\). Since \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\), it follows that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\). Thus \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\), so \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Since \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\) and \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\), we have \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Hence
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
If \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(a\) has order \(2m\), this implies \(2m\mid2n\), hence \(m\mid n\). Therefore the least positive such \(n\) is \(m\), so \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\). Because \(m\) is odd,
\[
a^m=(-(-a))^m=-(-a)^m\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
so \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). Now suppose \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\). Then
\[
(-a)^{2n}=a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p,
\]
so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\); write \(n=qm\). Then
\[
1\equiv a^n=(a^m)^q\equiv(-1)^q\pmod p.
\]
As \(p\) is odd, this forces \(q\) to be even. Thus \(2m\\mid n\). Since \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\), it follows that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\). Hence \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Thus \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\), while \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\) and \(p\) is odd, it follows that \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Therefore
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)\mid m\). Conversely, if \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m\), we have \(2m\mid2n\), so \(m\mid n\). Consequently \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\). Put \(b=-a\), so \(\operatorname{ord}_p(b)=m\) and \(a=-b\). Since \(m\) is odd,
\[
a^{2m}=(-b)^{2m}=b^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Now suppose \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(n\) is even, then \(b^n=(-1)^n a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid n\). Because \(m\) is odd and \(n\) is even, this gives \(2m\mid n\).

If \(n\) is odd, then \(b^n=(-1)^n a^n\equiv-1\pmod p\). Squaring gives \(b^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\), which would imply \(b^n\equiv1\pmod p\), a contradiction. Thus no odd \(n\) satisfies \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\).

Therefore every positive exponent \(n\) with \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\) is divisible by \(2m\), while \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). Hence \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\), so \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

problem.theorem: Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.
